description: Summary object returned by run_acquisition, also serialized into analysis_results['funnel_report'].
signature:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AcquisitionReport:
    run_id: str
    catalog_size: int
    candidate_count: int
    detail_fetched: int
    detail_failed: int
    reviews_fetched: int
    reviews_failed: int
    requests_made: int
    duration_seconds: float
    funnel: FunnelResult
docstring:
Outcome of one full acquisition stage run.

Attributes:
    run_id: The run this report belongs to.
    catalog_size: Total apps seen in the SteamSpy bulk catalog (FunnelResult.total_input).
    candidate_count: Survivors of coarse_filter (len(FunnelResult.candidates)).
    detail_fetched: appdetails fetches that returned success=true.
    detail_failed: appdetails fetches that returned success=false or a transport error.
    reviews_fetched: review-summary fetches that succeeded.
    reviews_failed: review-summary fetches that failed.
    requests_made: Total HTTP requests issued across all three sources (bulk pages + per-app details + per-app reviews).
    duration_seconds: Wall-clock time for the whole stage.
    funnel: The FunnelResult from coarse_filter.
postconditions: detail_fetched + detail_failed == candidate_count (every candidate is attempted exactly once)

edge_cases.expected_behavior: detail_fetched, detail_failed, reviews_fetched, reviews_failed are all 0; requests_made reflects only the bulk-catalog page requests
detail_fetched == 0, detail_failed == candidate_count; the stage still completes and returns a report rather than raising, per the invariant that a failed per-app fetch degrades that app, not the run

unit_tests.name: test_counts_are_internally_consistent
unit_tests.description: For a synthetic 20-app run with 3 failures each on details and reviews, fetched+failed sums match candidate_count for both.
